final.memo:
CoStar Group is a premier provider of commercial real estate information, yet its valuation is severely distorted by heavy, speculative investment in its residential platform [D01]. While the core commercial and Apartments.com businesses demonstrate robust growth and dominant market positions, the company's FY2024 operating margin sits at a negligible 0.17%, a stark contrast to high-quality data peers like MSCI, which operate at 53.5% [D02], [D06].

Our sum-of-the-parts analysis reveals an company with $2.25 billion in combined core commercial and apartments revenue that is being mispriced due to aggressive residential expansion [D02]. By moderating Homes.com investment and targeting a 35% operating margin, we believe the business can achieve significant earnings power [D01]. Applying a 25x EV/EBITDA multiple to this post-event earnings profile suggests an equity value of approximately $125 per share, representing a compelling risk/reward skew [D01], [D06].

The market currently overemphasizes residential growth at the expense of earnings quality, failing to appreciate the resilience of the core subscription base [D05]. We intend to engage privately with CEO Andy Florance and the board to drive capital discipline, specifically demanding transparency on ROIC for residential initiatives and the acceleration of the current $500 million buyback [D01], [D07]. Our role is to act as a catalyst for margin expansion; should the board ignore this mandate, we are prepared to escalate our involvement publicly [D01], [D05].

We recognize the risks associated with founder-led capital allocation, but the company’s $3.689 billion net cash position provides an effective floor of approximately $70.30 per share, limiting our downside [D04]. We are initiating a 5% position in the common stock, sized to reflect our conviction in the company’s core franchise and the upside from portfolio simplification [D01], [D05]. We will hedge our market-wide cyclicality risk with index puts and exit quickly if management demonstrates an inability to pivot away from value-destructive residential spending [D01], [D05].
